s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive ocular and musculoskeletal abnormalities with onset in adolescence
salient_findings: Hypermobility of shoulders, digits, and knees
Substantial optic nerve cupping and loss of neural rim tissue
key_facts: Age of onset: 13 years
Elevated intraocular pressure
Taller stature than relatives
Long fingers
Hypermobility of shoulders, digits, and knees
Family history negative for similar findings
Normal serial echocardiograms
Open iridocorneal angle in each eye
No Haab striae, buphthalmos, or high iris insertion
Subtle lens dislocation superonasally in the right eye at age 17
Lens dislocation in the left eye at age 32
Heterozygous variants in the LTBP2 gene
Optic nerve cupping and loss of neural rim tissue

shortlist.label: Weill-Marchesani syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Characterized by ectopia lentis, short stature is not a requirement and can have normal stature, and is associated with musculoskeletal abnormalities

shortlist.label: Homocystinuria
shortlist.why_kept: Causes ectopia lentis, elevated intraocular pressure, and can have tall stature and musculoskeletal abnormalities

shortlist.label: Marfan syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Characterized by tall stature, ectopia lentis, and musculoskeletal abnormalities, but often associated with cardiac abnormalities which are not present in this case

shortlist.label: Ehlers-Danlos syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Characterized by hypermobility of joints, skin hyperextensibility, and tissue fragility, and can have ocular abnormalities including ectopia lentis

shortlist.label: Stickler syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Characterized by ocular abnormalities including ectopia lentis, and can have musculoskeletal abnormalities and tall stature

raw.rationale: The combination of elevated intraocular pressure, lens dislocation, and skeletal features such as tall stature and joint hypermobility, along with the genetic findings of heterozygous variants in the LTBP2 gene, are most consistent with Weill-Marchesani syndrome.

rejected.label: Homocystinuria
rejected.why: Typically associated with intellectual disability, thromboembolism, and other systemic features not mentioned in the vignette

rejected.label: Marfan syndrome
rejected.why: Usually involves significant cardiovascular abnormalities, such as aortic root dilatation, which were not found on serial echocardiograms

rejected.label: Ehlers-Danlos syndrome
rejected.why: Characterized by skin hyperextensibility and tissue fragility, which are not described in the vignette

rejected.label: Stickler syndrome
rejected.why: Typically involves retinal detachment and a distinct facial appearance, which are not mentioned in the vignette
